title: Data structures: list, tuple, dict and set
summary: list, tuple, dict and set: when to use each one based on order, mutability, key lookup and uniqueness.

sections.definition: list: ordered, mutable sequence. tuple: ordered, immutable sequence (hashable if its contents are). dict: key → value, preserves insertion order and looks up in O(1). set: unique, unordered elements, membership in O(1).
sections.analogy: list is the line of orders at the counter; tuple, the coordinates printed on the receipt (they don't get rewritten); dict, the customer file indexed by ID number; set, the guest list where nobody appears twice.
sections.problem: Searching with in in a list scans everything (O(n)); in a set or dict it's almost instant. Using list for data that shouldn't change invites modifying it by mistake.
sections.code:example:
carrito = ["cafe", "taza", "cafe"]          # list: orden y duplicados
ubicacion = (4.4389, -75.2322)               # tuple: inmutable
stock = {"cafe": 12, "taza": 3}              # dict
categorias = {"bebidas", "accesorios"}       # set

stock.get("filtro", 0)     # 0, sin KeyError
"cafe" in stock            # True en O(1)
set(carrito)               # {'cafe', 'taza'}
precio, cantidad = (25_000, 2)   # desempaquetado de tupla
sections.bad:
ids_vip = [ ... 100_000 ids ... ]
for pedido in pedidos:
    if pedido.cliente_id in ids_vip:   # O(n) cada vez
        aplicar_descuento(pedido)

With 10,000 orders that's up to a billion comparisons.
sections.good:
ids_vip = set(lista_ids)
for pedido in pedidos:
    if pedido.cliente_id in ids_vip:   # O(1)
        aplicar_descuento(pedido)

Same code, different structure, orders of magnitude faster.
sections.bridge:typescript: list ≈ Array. dict ≈ object literal or Map, but keys must be hashable (you can't use a list as a key). set ≈ Set. tuple ≈ a TS readonly tuple, except the immutability really exists at runtime.
sections.interview: I use a list when I need an ordered collection that will change, a tuple when the data is fixed, like a record or a coordinate, and it can also be a dictionary key. A dictionary to look up by key in constant time and a set when I care about membership or removing duplicates. The choice affects performance: searching a list is O(n) and a set or dict is O(1) on average.
sections.myths:
• stock["filtro"] raises KeyError; in JS you'd get undefined. Use .get() when the key may be missing.
  • (1) is the number 1; the one-element tuple is (1,).
  • You use len(x), not x.length.
  • {} creates an empty dict, not a set. The empty set is set().

exercises.prompt: Classify each case with the most suitable structure.

items.text: History of an order's statuses, in order
Price of each product by its SKU code
Unique emails that already received the promo
Latitude and longitude of a store

items.code:
d = {"a": 1}
print(d.get("b"), len({1, 1, 2}))
items.why: .get() returns None if the key is missing, and the set {1, 1, 2} ends up with two elements.
